title: Reuse pays rent; changed weights invalidate an answer index
question: When does a reusable answer index repay its build cost, and what happens when its input changes?
method: Compare retained indexed and structural searches across tested batch sizes, then reuse a stale index after a weight change and test a guarded rebuild.
finding: Cold index loses to structural search at one query but wins at tested sizes 4,16,64. Changing one weight makes old index wrong on 23/64 queries; explicit identity comparison and rebuilding restore correctness.
claim_scope: Bounded historical result described by the retained source and receipts; no fresh scientific execution in this gathering.
limitations: One 16-position toy family; crossover only bracketed between 1 and 4.
Mutation detection/rebuild is an explicit scenario, not general cache service.
No total model-cost or general runtime benefit claim.
open_questions: How does the crossover change for other problem families when discovery, storage and maintenance costs are included?
